steps.content: As expected, the Underground Puppets fall before you, just as they always do. Its frame crumbles apart, dissolving into pale smoke before fading into dust in the air. Only a faint trace of that drifting voice remains, circling like the final echoes of a curse.

steps.speaker: Drifting Voice
steps.content: Heh heh... Go on... Keep struggling... Open those unseeing eyes of yours and behold...

steps.speaker: Drifting Voice
steps.content: Death is the only truth visible even to fools...
Daniel cowers at your feet, pupils trembling, both hands clutching his head in a desperate grip.

steps.speaker: Daniel
steps.content: I knew it, I knew it... I've been cursed. I'm gonna die, hehehe, hahaha...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What curse? That's Mania, not witchcraft. Forget all that superstitious nonsense. Get over here.
You pull him away from the lingering contamination, then beckon Schorl over. You have it run a quick scan on Daniel.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: His M-value remains within a safe range. Mr. Horston is merely in shock. He has not been harmed. You did a great job protecting him, Chief.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Good. We'll use this opportunity to officially declare him dead. Put out the word. The 9th Agency should be willing to place him under witness protection. He can lie low for a while.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And most importantly, run a full scan of the scene. Save all data of the traces.
It obediently turns back to get to work. You leave the scene to Schorl and send Daniel away. Then, you head to a quiet spot at the far end of the corridor and place a call.
[Scene Transition] Office

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Did it work? Was I helpful?

steps.speaker: Option
options: Of course, it's all thanks to you.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Haha, anyway, you did all the heavy lifting! I'm glad it worked! Once we've dealt with the real enemy, we'll throw a proper party in the council hall. When that day comes, just...

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Do as you see fit. I'll back you up on this.
The two of you share a laugh. You'll remember how to terrorize idiots with this line in the future. Quote it out of context. Play dumb afterward. Leave no evidence behind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It certainly caused quite a stir. The Sillage Society even attempted to wipe us out. The lead behind this man is probably useless now. The enemy's very vigilant. They won't hesitate to sever any unwanted ties immediately.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For now, please keep an eye on the people around you. Make note of anyone who starts making moves. I'll look into their ties to the Ring Research Institute on my end.
King agrees without hesitation.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: It's my honor to help you. Nonetheless...

Though the communication channel he's using is provided by Shattered Blade and specially encrypted to reduce the risk of interception, the Speaker still instinctively lowers his voice, carefully passing along the observations he's made within the council.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: There have been plenty of accusations against Isomer recently, some even harsher than those directed at you. But when the claims were investigated, none of the accusers could provide solid evidence, and some even became evasive when questioned further.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: The "suspicious projects" were investigated too, but she deflected every accusation, shifting the blame onto Former Director Professor Lambert, Nirvana, the Ring Research Institute, Paradeisos, the war, and even the accusers themselves.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I can imagine. The current Director doesn't seem to hide her ambition at all. She's probably made plenty of enemies. Yet she's held onto her position this whole time without anyone finding enough dirt to force her out. She must have other tricks up her sleeve.
You recall that moment...
[Flashback CG: Isomer's Scheme]

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You get your Black Ring, I get my seat. A perfect win-win. What do you say?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She prefers not to get her hands dirty herself. Instead, she identifies people's hidden desires and offers them a partnership, drawing them into her web in the process. Heh... If I'm being honest, I'd be embarrassed too if Lemma ever found out about the things I've been up to.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Now that's a real schemer. She's been playing this game for years, hasn't she? Despite all the enemies she's made and all the shady things she's done, she always manages to come out clean. She's clearly been ten steps ahead of everyone else the whole time, and she's meticulous about covering her tracks.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Or she might be backed by someone powerful.
You rub your fingertips together, watching the residual purple smoke dust gradually fade, your thoughts drifting to its owner—your true enemy.
And the person on the other end of the line seems to read your mind.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Watch yourself, Chief. No matter how you look at it, she's way too ambitious. Someone like that is dangerous. Proceed cautiously.
You smile. Elvira said the same thing. You make a mental note of the sincere warnings from your two friends.

steps.speaker: Option
options: "The rougher the sea, the higher the price of the fish."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And I've already secured the most important prize from this trip.
With that, you end the call with King and glance toward the other end of the corridor. Schorl has finished scanning and drifts leisurely back toward you.
Before it can finish its report, you are bombarded by notifications. You open them and find that they're from the technical experts up in the sky.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So eager, huh? Alright, here you go. Send the data, Schorl.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The contamination left clear residue at the scene, and it is directly related to the characteristics of Death's Mania and their core sorcery. Let's get this firsthand data to the technical experts. It should help refine their model and bring us closer to cracking the enemy's dimensional technology.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Understood. Transmission initiated. Progress: 13%, 18%, 23%...

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: I assumed you would return to the Observation Hub and deliver it to Lemma in person.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Analyzing my thought process again? Heh, well, you're right. I did want to do that. But right now, something more important requires my attention.
You look at the black bipyramid.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did the urgent meeting request I made two days ago get approved? ...You don't have anything else scheduled for him, right?
You pause to think, then add:

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I promise I won't lay a hand on him this time.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Of course. You've already proven yourself to be both rational and reliable. We trust you, and we depend on you. Everything we do is for the sake of the investigation into the Underground.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Progress: 100%. Data successfully transmitted to the Observation Hub. Your meeting request has also been approved. Shall we depart now?
[Scene Change]
You return once again to the 9th Agency's highest-security cell and see a familiar face.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Long time no see, Chief ${PlayerName}.
